trouble_paranoid.otherNightReminder: Before dawn, wake the paranoid and give them a "yes" (for drunk/poisoned) or "no" (for sober/healthy). This info might be wrong when they are drunk/poisoned at the moment. When the paranoid would have become drunk/poisoned/sober/healthy, this effect only takes effect at (next) dawn.

trouble_pastor.ability: Each night, ask for 1 info signal concerning tonight's or yesterday's death targets. (The info can only be conditional regarding alignment or type of others.)
trouble_pastor.otherNightReminder: Add a "killed" to each dying player and a "protected" to each player whose death is prevented by protection. Wake the Pastor (or let them visit you the next day). They show you one question whose answer must directly concern info about the players who either died or did not due to protection since last dawn. The question may not make or ask for assumptions about anything else than player alignment or character type, else you either give an empty answer (a maybe) or request a new question. The paster may ask for any 1 info signal directly & not more than 1 info signal.

trouble_patroness.ability: Each night, choose 1 alive player without outsider abilities (not yourself) who gets immune against wishes or changes caused by others until dusk. The Demon knows who.
trouble_patroness.otherNightReminder: Before the Demon acts, wake the Patroness and let them point at 1 alive player (not themself). Sleep. If this player has no outsider ability (i.e. no ability associated to a character in the script's outsider section), add the "blessed" to that player. Wishes and state or property changes do not affect the player with "blessed" reminder, if they orignate from a player without "blessed" reminder. (E.g. they don't die from other players.) However, state or property effects may still end regularly (and won't be removed by the blessing). Players with "blessed" reminder are still affected by effects from actions and abilities they use. When the Demon wakes, show them that the Patroness chose the player with the "blessed" reminder.

trouble_physician.ability: Each night, choose 1 player to cure persistent action, ability, property defects and protect against new ones this cycle.
trouble_physician.otherNightReminder: Remove the "treated". Early at night, the Physician chooses 1 player (even themself). Mark them with "treated". Persistent action, ability and property defects are removed (remove its reminders, else add a "cured" if necessary). Obtaining new such defects is prevented this cycle.

trouble_pope.ability: Once per game at night, choose 1 player (incl. yourself) who learns this & cannot die before you. The demon might kill you even when protected. This ability is sober.
trouble_pope.otherNightReminder: Whenever the Demon chose the Pope, decide whether the Pope dies, no matter their reminders or protection abilities (the probability of dying should be higher without protection). If no player has the "holy" reminder, allow the Pope to choose 1 player (themself included). If they chose one: Sleep. Mark the player with the chosen player with "holy" reminder. Wake the chosen Player and show them, they were chosen by the Pope. Sleep. In the rest of the game: when the player with "holy" reminder would die, they do not. When the pope dies, remove the "holy" reminder.

trouble_poppysnitch.ability: Minions & Demons do not know each other but get 3 independent bluffs. If you die, minions & demons get to know each other that night.
trouble_poppysnitch.firstNightReminder: Do not inform the Demon/Minions who each other are but prepare 3 bluffs independently for each evil person. The bluffs may overlap.
trouble_poppysnitch.otherNightReminder: If the Poppy Grower has died, show the Minions/Demon who each other are.

trouble_prodigy.ability: You have +N ≥ 2 Townsfolk (of which ≥ 1 queries no properties) & +N/2 Outsider characters. Evils get +((N-1)/2) Minion characters.
trouble_prodigy.firstNightReminder: Decide which Townsfolk and Outsider abilities the prodigy obtains. At least one Townsfolk ability gets and infers no information. Compute the compensatory number of evil characters and assign these characters to already evil players. Evil Townsfolk or outsider who get a minion ability become a minion and are going to get minion info. Minion abilities can be distributed among multiple evil players. Wake up the Prodigy and show them that they are the Prodigy followed by the sequence of all characters that they have. Put all these characters to the Prodigy player in the Grimoire. Rest: See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_prodigy.otherNightReminder: Play the abilities of the Prodigy in the correct night order. When an ability would be used, wake up the Prodigy show them the character token (for the ability) and play the ability. Sleep. Whenever any ability queries or refers to the character of the Prodigy, this is not the Prodigy character but the story teller must choose one of the characters that helps the Prodigy's team most.

jinxes.reason: The Spy does not see the extra characters of the Prodigy.
The Widow does not see the Prodigy, only 1 extra character they have.

trouble_prophet.ability: You start knowing an inactive rule. At day, if you declare it correctly: even after you died, it is active & another good & evil player learn your character until dawn.
trouble_prophet.firstNightReminder: Invent a funny or interesting game rule which fits to your character setup. It should be sufficiently short and simple so that the Prophet can memorize it correctly. At night 1 or day 1, tell the Prophet the game rule. Whenever the Prophet asks you, restate the game rule again.
trouble_prophet.otherNightReminder: If the Prophet approximately stated the game rule correctly at the last day, and did not make multiple different declarations, register a game rule exactly corresponding to what the Prophet declared. If the declared game rule deviates too much from your original intent, ignore it. If you accept the declaration, when it is sufficiently close, wake up 1 good & 1 evil player (sequentially, not simulatenously). Show them who the Prophet is.

trouble_psychatrist.ability: Each night, choose 1 player to cure their persistent social, perceptional and behavioral impairments & prevent new ones this cycle.
trouble_psychatrist.otherNightReminder: Remove the "treated". Early at night, the Psychatrist chooses 1 player (even themself). Mark them with "treated". Their persistent social conditions and ability manipuatlions are removed (remove its reminders, else add a "cured" if necessary). Obtaining new such impairments is prevented this cycle.

trouble_psychic.ability: Each dawn, learn all players (max. 2) whose abilities interacted with you at night. If it's only 1, learn a false 2nd.
trouble_psychic.otherNightReminder: Add the "psyched" to any 2 other players who choose, see or learn info about the Psychic player (even drunk/poisoned). If it's only 1, add 1 false "psyched" such that there are 2 or 0 reminders. At the night's end, wake the Psychic and point to all players with "psyched" reminder. Remove the "psyched" s.

trouble_puppeteer.ability: Each night, choose 2 players to swap accountability & registration. Character+alignment swaps if 1 of them dies self-accountably. You die if both have died.
trouble_puppeteer.otherNightReminder: At dawn, if there is no "genuine" reminder, let the Puppeteer choose 2 players (themself included). Move the "swapped" reminders to the chosen players. Players with "swapped" reminder account for the other player's actions/ability uses and registers as them. If a player with "swapped" reminder dies and accounts for it (considering the swap) then add the "genuine" reminder to both players. Both players with "swapped" and "genuine" learn their new character and alignment. If both players with "swapped" reminder are dead, the Puppeteers dies. When the Puppeteer died, remove the "swapped" and "genuine" reminder and the previously swapped players learn their original character+alignment from the girmoire.

trouble_puzzledrunk.ability: You have another drunk character. Once per game, 1 good player may guess you. If right, they learn the actual Demon player, else get false info (not themself).
trouble_puzzledrunk.firstNightReminder: Choose a character token that the Puzzledrunk should have and see initially. Put it into the bag, not the Puzzledrunk character. This allows you to put up to one illegal pair of characters in the bag. The Puzzledrunk player will play this character but it's ability will always be drunk. Add the "Puzzled" to this player. Also choose a player who may guess the Puzzledrunk. Add the "Puzzler" to them. Wake that player to inform them that the Puzzledrunk is in play.
trouble_puzzledrunk.otherNightReminder: At most the player with "Puzzler" reminder may guess the Puzzledrunk. You should refuse an answer to them, if they are the wrong player. If they guessed publicly or privately, privately tell them a player name. If their guess is right, you give a correct player name, else an incorrect one (but not the name of the asking player).

jinxes.reason: The Puzzledrunk is not a Legion(atic). When the sober+healthy Puzzledrunk guesses right, they learn a 3rd non-Legion player.
The Trustmaker shows the Puzzledrunk player correctly as the Puzzledrunk.

trouble_rationalist.ability: You are Atheist. The Story Teller modifies ≤ 1 player's abilities, misregisters ≤ X players as evil minions/demons, fakes minion signals & has 1 demon ability. [X = regular # of evil]
trouble_rationalist.firstNightReminder: Choose 1 person to whom you add unknown rules and modifications whose effect holds while this person has their abilities. Choose at most the regular number of evil players to let them always register as Minions + 1 Demon to other abilities. You may fake the public or private Minion signals that the Minion abilities emit. Choose 1 demon ability for yourself. Nothing else is manipulated.
trouble_rationalist.otherNightReminder: Remain consist and don't manipulate more than you are allowed to. If the manipulated player has no ability anymore, their manipulation is gone. When the game ends, explain what manipulation and rules you have chosen.

trouble_robber.ability: At night, if you account for killing the last alive Minion, you learn the Demon player. You know the Clan Boss player.
trouble_robber.firstNightReminder: If a Clan Boss is in play, wake up the Robber and show them the Clan Boss player with the Clan Boss character.
trouble_robber.otherNightReminder: If the Robber is alive, nominated and executed the last alive Minion today or tonight, wake up the Robber before dawn and show them the Demon player. If a Clan Boss is created in the mid of the game, the Robber learns this.

trouble_samurai.ability: Each night, choose 1 player who dies if it is an outsider. You are of Townsfolk+Outsider type. [? Samurai]
trouble_samurai.firstNightReminder: Consider that a Samurai can be counted as Outsider or as Townsfolk for the setup. During the game, a Samurai counts as both. If both are in conflict, you decide one of both for the situation.
trouble_samurai.otherNightReminder: Let the Samurai point at 1 player. Maintain a histogram of Outsider choices made by good and by evil Samurai players. For each of both histograms, if at least 1 Outsider was chosen, kill 1 of the Outsiders with most votes within the histogram. The death triggers immediately.

trouble_sectarian.ability: Nobody knows: you win with good. Your evil character works abnormally. You might register as good character to 1 other Townsfolk.
trouble_sectarian.firstNightReminder: The Sectarian might replace an actual minion or demon. Determine a discernible modification for the evil character shown to the Sectarian player. (It must consistently work abnormally.) Give correct minion/demon info to the Sectarian and treat the Sectarian as evil minion/demon. You might treat the Sectarian as Townsfolk or Outsider for 1 other Townsfolk players
trouble_sectarian.otherNightReminder: Play the modified ability of the Sectarian. The Sectarian registers as evil character and might register as Townsfolk or Outsider to 1 other Townsfolk player.

trouble_shaman.ability: Each night, the Demon can have 1 target. If you guess all demon targets, you learn all alive characters and bluffs. (The Demon might know you are in play.)
trouble_shaman.otherNightReminder: The Shaman ability allows the Demon to choose 0 or 1 player if they had no target tonight. At dawn, let the Shaman guess ≥ 0 players, mark them with "guessed". If all guessed players are the ones with Demonic target reminder, nod your head "yes". Then at dawn, show all characters and your given bluffs that all alive players use. Else shake your head "no". Remove the "guess" s.

trouble_sleuth.ability: You start knowing a not-in-play good character. Each night, choose 1 player: you learn an actual good character of them or of nobody.
trouble_sleuth.firstNightReminder: Show the Sleuth a good character that is no demon bluff & nobody actually has (no misregistration).
trouble_sleuth.otherNightReminder: The Sleuth points at 1 alive/dead player. If Townsfolk or Outsider, you might show the player's actual good character (no misregistration). Else show a good not-in-play character.

trouble_smartypants.ability: You start knowing 2 players with different actual character type & 1 actual ability or character among them.
trouble_smartypants.firstNightReminder: Choose 2 players who actually have at least 1 pair of different character types among them. (Ignore misregistrations.) Add the "Smarts Yes" and "Smarts No" to them. Wake the Smartypants and point at the players with "Smarts Yes" and "Smarts No" reminder. Also show the character token of one ability or character of the player with "Smarts Yes" reminder.

trouble_soulkeeper.ability: Each night, choose ≤ 1 player who, if dead, takes+adds your abilities+life, or, if alive, returns all abilities to you when they die. Meanwhile you cannot act/wake.
trouble_soulkeeper.firstNightReminder: Mark the Soulkeeper player with the "soulkeeper" reminder. Rest: see Other Night Reminder.
trouble_soulkeeper.otherNightReminder: When a player with "soulchosen" reminder exists in the Grimoire don't wake up the Soulkeeper. Otherwise, let the Soulkeeper choose a player. When they choose themself, let them use their Soulkeeper abilities. They can use abilities of all players marked with "soulcaught" in the grimoire. Whenever the character would take effect at night, also wake the Soulkeeper then, play the ability and sleep. If the Soulkeeper chooses no player, do not wake them anymore this night. If the Soulkeeper chooses a dead player, move a "soulkeeper" reminder to the new person and move their shroud to the previous soulkeeper. Only one player may have the "soulkeeper" reminder. This player must be declared to be be resurrected at dawn. If the Soulkeeper chooses an alive player, mark them with the "soulchosen" reminder. Whenever a Soulkeeper character would be created mid-game, move the "soulchosen" reminder to that player if a "soulkeeper" marked player exists otherwise use a "soulkeeper" reminder for the player. Whenever a soulchosen player dies, replace their "soulchosen" reminder with the "soulcaught" reminder. When the Soulkeeper really dies, remove all soulchosen, soulcaught and soulkeeper reminders from the grimoire.

trouble_soulmate.ability: Each night, choose ≤ 1 person who has their abilities when dead & triggers no effects on death. When you chose you die and lose all abilities! Fixed alignment!
trouble_soulmate.otherNightReminder: Let the soulmate choose at most 1 person after demon but before minions. When the soulmate chose, it is like the demon tried to kill them. Independent of the success of death, this soulmate loses all abilities. At the onset of the vessel effect – as soon as the vessel dies – tell them that the Soulmate chose them. (Do this even if they chose themself.)

trouble_survivor.ability: You start knowing 1 good player. At night, after a player dies whose character you claimed publicly before they did, learn 1 more dead player's character.
trouble_survivor.firstNightReminder: Show 1 good player to the Survivor. (Not the character.)
trouble_survivor.otherNightReminder: When the Survivor publicly and most recently has claimed a character which coincides with the registered character of another alive player, move the (unflipped) "claimed" to that player. If another player publicly claims their own character, add a flipped down "claimed" to that player. Do not add a "claimed" reminder if the player already has a un-/flipped "claimed" reminder. If a player's registered character changes, remove any "claimed" s from this player. If a player with the (unflipped) "claimed" reminder dies, add the "survived" to them and remove the (unflipped) "claimed". At night, if there is a "survived" reminder, wake the Survivor up and show them 1 dead player together with the player's character. (This is usually valuable info except if the survivor passed the condition effortlessly, e.g. with a drunk Demon). Sleep. Then remove the "survived" s. Remove any "claimed" or "survived" reminders when the Survivor changes character or resurrects.

trouble_theist.ability: Players can cheat rules. Players win if not caught cheating. Heretics & Atheists don't work. Everyone loses If you execute the story teller. Only executions kill you.

trouble_therapist.ability: Each night, learn whether your chosen states are present for among all or 1 chosen player. Once per game, learn the complete state of 1 chosen player.
trouble_therapist.otherNightReminder: Let the therapist point to a player, let them choose any combination of state properties to query. If any of these properties is present, give a "yes" else a "no". If they point to the story teller, give one answer for all players.

trouble_vagrant.ability: You might count as Outsider or Traveller all the game. [-0 or -1 Outsiders,? Vagrants]
trouble_vagrant.firstNightReminder: If the Vagrant should count as Outsider, add the "Outsider" reminder at the player in the grimoire, or the "Traveller" reminder respectively. Vagrants may replace actual Outsiders.

trouble_vampirehunter.ability: You start knowing 1 demon character in play. Each night°, choose ≤ ¼ of alive players. You learn what characters account for their death until dusk.
trouble_vampirehunter.firstNightReminder: Show the Vampire Hunter 1 demon character in play.
trouble_vampirehunter.otherNightReminder: Before players can kill, wake up the Vampire Hunter. Show the Vampire any character concerning players who are marked "anointed" and "killed by ‹character›". Remove any "anointed" and "killed by" reminders. Let the Vampire Hunter choose ≤ ¼ of alive players, i.e. 1 for 4 to 7, 2 for 8 to 11, 3 for 12 to 15 alive players. Mark them with the "anointed" reminder. Later during the night or day, when any anointed player dies, mark them with a "killed by ‹character›" reminder using the character of the responsible player.

trouble_villagegargoyle.ability: On night ≥ 2, when your team has majority, you are demon-killed & become not-in-play Townsfolk. Give it to 1 chosen player, once your team loses majority. Your character lives even if dead.
trouble_villagegargoyle.firstNightReminder: Choose a not-in-play Townsfolk for the Gargoyle or let a dedicated Gargoyle player choose one before the game. In night 1, the Gargoyle only has the Gargoyle character.
trouble_villagegargoyle.otherNightReminder: Even if the Village Gargoyle player is dead, the Village Gargoyle character still lives (and their Townsfolk character might as well). The first time on night ≥ 2, if the team of the Village Gargoyle has more alive players than the other team(s), the Village Gargoyle dies at night, publicly(!), and the Demon skips their action of that night. Additionally: add a Townsfolk character by adding its token to the Village Gargoyle token in the Grimoire. The first time on night ≥ 2 when the Village Gargoyle is not part of the majority team anymore, wake them to choose 1 other (dead or alive) player. The Village Gargoyle's Townsfolk character moves to the chosen player whose previous character is replaced. If it is a Demon player with active ability, yet another alive player becomes the evil Demon of equal charater instead.

trouble_anarchist.ability: You have every alignment & character type unless you die. You register like the interacting player. Demon abilities & story teller choices don't kill you. You get 1 bluff.
trouble_anarchist.firstNightReminder: Show 1 good bluff character to the Anarchist. It might coincide with the bluff of someone else.
trouble_anarchist.flavor: It's all about life, no alignment, no rulers.

trouble_bipartisan.ability: You are not Townsfolk & cannot die from executions or Demons & cannot call for & support ballots positively. You might be anti.
trouble_bipartisan.firstNightReminder: Decide whether the Bipartisan should be anti the whole game or not. (A normal one is not executed and demon-killed and cannot execute others. An anti-one is assassinated during the game instead of the death of an executee or demon victim but may nominate even if dead, prolonging the game after all goods are dead.) If yes, add the "permanent-anti" to the player. Rest: See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_bipartisan.otherNightReminder: A Bipartisan with "permanent-anti" reminder has the anti state. If the Bipartisan is anti, they might be assassinated instead of 1 executee or 1 demon victim being killed. Dead or alive players may claim the Bipartisan character at day to call for ballots, no matter their state, but if the player is not an anti Bipartisan, the ballot cannot succeed. The anti Bipartisan's call for a ballot is always treated like a valid call for the ballot and their vote/support for a ballot is always valid and counts positively. On the other hand, normal Bipartisans don't register as players towards any ballot rules, even calls and support for exiles, as long as their vote would count positively. Hence, nominations and votes of normal Bipartisan players covertly fail and get ignored (as if not happened). If a normal Bipartisan is executed or would be killed by the Demon, they don't die. If an anti Bipartisan is in play, the game ends, if only ≤ 2 alive players are not normal Bipartisan players (or if remaining good team votes are ≤ evil team votes). If no anti Bipartisan is in play the game ends when only one team is still alive excluding normal Bipartisan players.

trouble_buddha.ability: Once per game, even dead, if you correctly guess to be a given character, you are sober & will win (independently). If false, you are drunk. You might: be evil or register as Buddha. [+1 arbitary player]
trouble_buddha.firstNightReminder: Choose any non-script or in-script ability for the Buddha or one that is fake or manipulated (which does not exist). Choose the ability's character or a character that allows for confusion with the Buddha's ability and show this character to the Buddha in this night. (The Buddha must know this character.) The Buddha player may register as or replace a player in the setup if and only if their alignment and character/ability is equal to those that the player would have. The Buddha may be a secret Traveller. Give them an alignment that fits their character. If the Buddha registers as their character, put the character token next to the Buddha token in the grimoire. Rest: See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_buddha.otherNightReminder: The Buddha may guess any time but does not guess at night. If the Buddha guessed correctly, add the "enlightened" to the Buddha player. If the Buddha guessed falsely, add the "benighted" to the Buddha player. The "benighted" reminder is equal to being "drunk". The "enlightened" reminder means, the Buddha player and ability cannot get drunk anymore. When the game ends and the Buddha has the "enlightened" reminder, they win regardless of who else wins.

trouble_daimyou.ability: If a good non-traveller accounts for your death, 1 player dies each dusk until the accountable is dead. ≥ 1 alive Samurai learn your death. You might register as evil.
trouble_daimyou.firstNightReminder: Contemplate what players would see the Daimyou as evil player.
trouble_daimyou.otherNightReminder: If a Daimyou died at the previous day, inform ≥ 1 Samurai about it at this night. You at least inform a Samurai that does not account for the Daimyou death. Inform them at the earliest point at night after the Daimyou's death which may be before or after that Samurai chooses 1 player. If the Daimyou dies and a good player – not a traveller – accounts for it, add the "massacre" reminder to that player. Of all alive Samurai, add the "know death" reminder to at least 1 Samurai who has no "massacre" reminder, otherwise to the alive Samurai with "massacre" reminder. After the Daimyou death at night, notify the Samurai players with "know death" reminder – and optionally more Samurai – about the Daimyou's death. At dusk, when a player has the "massacre" reminder, choose one player who dies. Add a shroud. If this is a notified Samurai, notify them of the Daimyou death even when they died at dusk. At dawn, remove any "know death" reminders. When the player with "massacre" reminder dies, remove the reminder.

trouble_deathgargoyle.ability: You start as covertly dead. Once per game, you get alive if your team loses majority. If you die, choose 1 alive player to kill at night: if a demon, 1 other alive player gets evil+this demon.
trouble_deathgargoyle.firstNightReminder: If the Gargoyle is part of the majority Team, they are dead from the start. Don't add a Shroud, don't show the death publicly. Otherwise, add a "vivid" to the player.
trouble_deathgargoyle.otherNightReminder: If the Gargoyle's team turned from a majority to non-majority, add the "vivid" to the player. Don't declare anything. If the Gargoyle is attacked while not having the "vivid" reminder, it doesn't kill. If the Gargoyle is killed while having the "vivid" reminder, remove the "vivid" & make the Gargoyle die normally and publicly & in the next occasion at night, let the Gargoyle choose 1 alive player who dies. If it is an active Demon player, yet another alive player becomes an evil Demon of equal character.

trouble_fan.ability: Once per game, guess 1 of 3 initially seen minion characters to be not in play. If you are right, you get evil + this minion, else you get good. You are an Ogre.
trouble_fan.firstNightReminder: Choose N ≤ 3 actually in-play minion characters and 3 - N minions which are not (and possibly a character that other players believe to be in play). Show these 3 to the Fan. Also: let them choose 1 player for their Ogre ability. They get the chosen player's alignment and are informed about it.
trouble_fan.otherNightReminder: At day, when the Fan visited you and made a minion guess: when it was right, they get to see the minion character + evil alignment tonight. Change their character to the minion. Otherwise they get to see a good alignment. Indicate the player's good alignment in the Grimoire by unflipping the Fan token. If they got a new alignment, remove the "Fan Friend" reminder (the Ogre ability is lost).

trouble_fraudster.ability: If you are "mad" about being no Townsfolk, the execution might not kill this cycle, even if you died.
trouble_fraudster.otherNightReminder: Even if the Fraudster died, at day, remove any "Void Execution". If the Fraudster has been mad about being no Townsfolk, you might add 1 "Void Execution" to the Grimoire. If this reminder is in place, an execution triggers no death.

trouble_impersonator.ability: You start knowing a character nobody knows is not in play. If you convince someone to be it until the end, you win independently. The Story Teller might help you. You might be an evil Minion.
trouble_impersonator.firstNightReminder: Add the character to the Impersonator that they are tasked to perform. The Impersonator registers as the alignment from this character.
trouble_impersonator.otherNightReminder: At the end of the game, let players guess the character of the Impersonator. If at least 1 player guesses right (and is certain), the Impersonator wins even if they would not. The Impersonator can let the story teller send signals, messages to invidividual players or declarations to everyone. Either, they arrange these messages in a private talk at day with you, or uses a prepared message or gestures for you at night.

trouble_limpet.ability: On your 1st night, choose 3 players. They learn it. If none of them is present, you must stay paralyzed. Something dire might happen if you cheat.
trouble_limpet.firstNightReminder: Let them choose 3 players. Add the "gang" reminder to each of them. Sleep. Wake up each player with "gang" reminder and show them that the Limpet character chose them.
trouble_limpet.otherNightReminder: If you catch the Limpet to privately reveal game info when no player with "gang" reminder is around (or someones snitches on them), you may choose a bad consequence to happen for the Limpet's team. (See Almanac)

trouble_lover.ability: On your 1st night, choose 1 player (not yourself) who gets to know you. You share the alignment & death with each other, even if dead.
trouble_lover.firstNightReminder: Let the Lover choose 1 player (not themself). Add the "beloved" to this player and inform the Lover about their alignment. Inform the player with "beloved" reminder that the Lover has chosen them. Rest: See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_lover.otherNightReminder: At night or day, the Lover (even if dead) registers as the alignment of the player with "beloved" reminder. If the Lover would change alignment, the player with "beloved" reminder gets this alignment. When the Lover dies (even after being resurrected) or the player with "beloved" reminder dies, both players die together.

trouble_masterhora.ability: Each extra execution swaps the next night with its following day, ≤ current outsider number of times. The game can end only at dusk or dawn.
trouble_masterhora.otherNightReminder: Count the number of players "N" who register as outsiders at dusk and add a "‹N› outsiders" to Master Hora. At day, when someone is executed, add a "skip ‹X›" to Master Hora where X is the execution's ordinal number (the first execution has X = 0). If X = N, also force the day to end. At dawn, if Master Hora has a "skip ‹X›" reminder where X ≥ 1, replace the "skip ‹X›" reminder with a "skip ‹X-1›" and repeat the whole night phase again in correct night phase order. Else, end the night. You might end the night (but not the day) at a dusk (before the next night) if a team has won.

jinxes.reason: Master Hora shifts a night only when a good player is executed. If Leviathan chooses Master Hora at night, they die.
Master Hora shifts a night only when a good player is executed. If Diabolus chooses Master Hora at night, they die.

trouble_maverick.ability: When you learn that you died, publicly choose 1 alive player: if they are evil, you become a Heretic at dusk or dawn and the opposite team learns this.
trouble_maverick.otherNightReminder: If the Maverick has died, let them choose 1 player. If the chosen player is evil, the Maverick turns into a Heretic next dusk (if good) or next dawn (if evil). At least all players of the opposite team learn about this event.

trouble_nihilist.ability: You are anti, have ≥ 1 ability & are of the character types of abilities you have. You have any character type. [? Nihilists]
trouble_nihilist.firstNightReminder: Choose ≥ 1 script abilities of any character type and add the characters to the Nihilist player in the Grimoire. Show the Nihilist that they are those characters. Rest: See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_nihilist.otherNightReminder: Play each ability of the Nihilist when that ability would appear at night (start showing the character to play each time). But, falsify any clauses, adverbs, numbers and non-info and non-player-state outputs when you run any of their abilities. You may choose any arbitrary interpretation of negation for any clause, as long as the result will be different from the non-anti version.
trouble_nihilist.flavor: Everything is nothing and nothing is everything.

trouble_pinocchio.ability: At nominations, if you lie about the game, the demon acts twice tonight. If executed: choose 1 alive neighbor to become Pinocchio, you (& another neighbor might) become a Vagrant.
trouble_pinocchio.otherNightReminder: At dawn, if Pinocchio convincingly spread misinformation during any nomination, add the "liar" reminder to the Pinocchio player (remove the reminder when the Pinocchio debunked it or acknowledged the mistake sincerely), otherwise remove it. When a Demon player acted and the living Pinocchio player has a "liar" reminder, let the Demon act again (consecutively). At night after their execution, let Pinocchio choose 1 neighbour among the alive-registering players but not Travellers (it skips any dead neighbours). If they did not choose a valid player, shake the head and let them choose again. E.g. they might have chosen a Traveller Vagrant or the Frankenstein who covertly registers as dead. The Pinocchio player changes to a Vagrant. Inform them. Sleep. The chosen player changes their Character to Pinocchio. Wake up this player and inform them. The other alive neighbour might transform into a Vagrant. If they do, wake them and inform them and sleep. Avoid this if it would end the game.

trouble_punk.ability: You play a drunk not-in-play ability (no Outsider). You are or register as its character type. If you are "checked" by a good ability, + ≤1 player dies at night.
trouble_punk.firstNightReminder: If the Punk plays a drunk Demon, the Demon might learn the Punk player. (Like Lunatic.) See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_punk.otherNightReminder: Play the Punk's drunk ability. At day or night, if a good ability "checks" the Punk – i.e. chooses them for an effect which is conditional w.r.t. player properties – add the "checked" to the center. If the "checked" reminder exists, choose a player to die. Allow for false conclusions with the kill. If the Punk has a drunk Demon ability, the Demon might learn who the Punk chooses tonight before the Demon chooses. (Like Lunatic.) Remove the "checked"

trouble_romantic.ability: At the end of game, if you live you lose. Good abilities don't kill you. You have Victim + Maverick ability. [≥ 2 Outsiders]
trouble_romantic.firstNightReminder: You can only use the Romantic, if there is yet another Outsider in the setup. Wake 1 Minion, show them the 'This character selected you' card and the Romantic token. Add the "chases Romantic" to them in the Grimoire. Wake 1 genuinely good Townsfolk, show them the Romantic player and character. (See Victim in Almanac.)
trouble_romantic.otherNightReminder: If the player with "chases Romantic" reminder is a minion and guesses a player as Romantic publicly today, add the "guessed Romantic" to the guessed player in the Grimoire (if this player is alive at that moment), otherwise it is put in the center. If a player with Lycanthrope ability chooses the Romantic, nothing happens. At (or after) dawn, if the Romantic player has the "guessed Romantic" reminder, the team of the Romantic loses & the other team wins. Remove the "chases Romantic" and "guessed Romantic" reminders if the Romantic character is removed. If the Romantic has died, let them choose a player. If this player is evil, the Maverick's penality triggers: they turn into a Wicked and at least all opposite alignment players learn it, at dawn or dusk. When the game ended and the Romantic is alive, the Romantic loses.

trouble_schizo.ability: You have any townsfolk or minion ability & alignment but you get false character – & possibly alignment – signals about yourself & possibly others.

trouble_siamesetwin.ability: You & your Twin know each other. You both share player state, properties & registration but act independently, even if dead.
trouble_siamesetwin.firstNightReminder: Early at night 1, choose 1 player as the Twin of the Siamese Twin. Mark the chosen player with "Siamese Twin". Show player, character and alignment of their Twin player to the Siamese Twin. The player marked "Siamese Twin" learns to be the twin of the Siamese Twin. (Don't make eye contact.) After the Twin acted at night, wake the Siamese if applicable and let them act too.
trouble_siamesetwin.otherNightReminder: Replay property signals or abilities of the player with "Siamese Twin" reminder for the Siamese. Both Siamese Twin players both have the union of their single player states.

trouble_sickener.ability: 1 player is sick since dawn 1. You start knowing their character & learn when they die. You might be a Townsfolk. [+1 arbitrary character+alignment]
trouble_sickener.firstNightReminder: Prepare the setup by replacing any 1 other character (and their alignment), not the Demon, with any character and any alignment. At dawn 1 (after the first night), add the "sickened" reminder to the affected player and show the sick character to the Sickener. Wake up the Sickener and show them the sickened player's character.
trouble_sickener.otherNightReminder: If the Sickener has their ability, don't wake up the player with "sickened" reminder, treat their day actions like a bluff and let their nominations fail covertly or overtly after the ballot with no reason. When the sickened player dies, wake up the Sickener at night. (You may show a death signal.)

trouble_traitor.ability: Each night, your alignment changes. Once per game, you may choose to not change alignment at night. You are an Ogre.
trouble_traitor.firstNightReminder: Play the Ogre ability: let them choose 1 player. Copy their alignment to the Traitor player. (Evil alignment flips the character token upside down.) Optionally, you may add the "Traitor friend" reminder to the chosen player and indicate the Traitor's alignment inversion by flipping their character token upside down. Rest: see Other Night Reminder.
trouble_traitor.otherNightReminder: If the Traitor has no "used" reminder: wake up the Traitor, if they show "yes", add the "used" reminder to them in the grimoire. Else if they show "no", rotate their character token by 180°. Show them their new alignment. Sleep. Whenever the Traitor's character token points upside down, it counts as opposite to their natural alignment. Remove their reminders when they resurrect.

trouble_victim.ability: If the 1 Minion (who knows you are in play) guesses you (once), your team loses at dawn. 1 genuinely good Townsfolk starts knowing you. [≥ 2 Outsiders]
trouble_victim.firstNightReminder: You can only use the Victim, if there is yet another Outsider in the setup. Wake 1 Minion, show them the 'This character selected you' card and the Victim token. Add the "chases Victim" to them in the Grimoire. Wake 1 genuinely good Townsfolk, show them the Victim player and character.
trouble_victim.otherNightReminder: If the player with "chases Victim" reminder is a minion and guesses a player as Victim publicly today, add the "guessed Victim" to the guessed player in the Grimoire (if this player is alive at that moment), otherwise it is put in the center. If a player with Lycanthrope ability chooses the Victim, nothing happens. At (or after) dawn, if the Victim player has the "guessed Victim" reminder, the team of the Victim loses & the other team wins. Remove the "chases Victim" and "guessed Victim" reminders if the Victim character is removed.

trouble_werwolfalpha.ability: Each night, you & evil learn if your chosen character is in play, OR each night, use Lycanthrope. The demon learns the chosen evil player. You register as evil.
trouble_werwolfalpha.firstNightReminder: Acts before the demon. Wake the Werwolf Alpha and show the script with characters. After they chose, signal a "yes" or "no". Sleep. Then wake the demon, show them the Werwolf Alpha character, then the chosen character and a "yes" or "no". If an evil player has this character, show the demon this player. Sleep. If an evil player has this character, also wake them up and show the Werwolf Alpha character to them. Sleep.
trouble_werwolfalpha.otherNightReminder: After waking up the Werwolf Alpha, allow them to choose a character or a player. When choosing a character, repeat what the First Night Reminder mentions. Otherwise, play the Lycanthrope ability. If Lycanthrope has been used and the demon is woken up to choose, show them the Werwolf Alpha character and point to the chosen player. Finish the demon's ability as normal. Sleep.

trouble_wicked.ability: Whoever wins, loses & whoever loses, wins, even if you are dead, except if the Story Teller is executed.

jinxes.reason: There is at least 1 not-in-play outsider.
Both characters are not in play together.
Both characters are not in play together.
Both characters are not in play together.
Pit-Hag cannot make a Wicked.

trouble_wicked.flavor: But many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first. (Matthew 30:19)

trouble_witcher.ability: You start knowing 1 special Jinx. While you are dead: the special jinx is active when it would not & if it is already active, it is negated instead.
trouble_witcher.firstNightReminder: Choose one of the existing active jinxes or invent a new one and inform the Witcher of this jinx as their special jinx. Add the "hexed" reminder to the grimoire character which is the source of the special Jinx. Remember this Jinx somewhere.
trouble_witcher.otherNightReminder: If the Witcher has a shroud reminder, check if their special Jinx for the player with "hexed" reminder has necessary conditions and characters satisfied. If yes, interpret the special Jinx as negated in any way that you like. If no, treat the special Jinx of the hexed player as active, as if the conditions and characters for it are satisfied.

trouble_agitator.ability: An evil starts knowing 1 good player who cannot be chosen by evil killing abilities. If this player nominates and executes more than everyone else, your team wins.
trouble_agitator.firstNightReminder: Choose 1 player who might be able to nominate more often than all others. Wake the Agitator (if evil) or an evil player and point at this player. Add the "agitated" to that player. Rest: See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_agitator.otherNightReminder: Whenever an evil ability chooses the player with "agitated" reminder, where this choice could possibly kill the player, the Story Teller refuses the choice and prompts to choose again. As soon as there is no player in the game that could nominate & execute as many players as the player with "agitated" reminder has already done, end the game and declare that evil wins (if good has not won by now).

trouble_angelofdeath.ability: Each night, if you choose ≤ ¼ of other alive players (no demon): they cannot die tonight & others attacking them are counterattacked, but if not, you kill yourself.
trouble_angelofdeath.otherNightReminder: At the start of the night, if there is a "countered" reminder and no "attacked" reminder, the Angel of Death kills themself. Remove any "countered" and "attacked" s. Before the demon(s) kill, if ≥ 4 players are alive, wake up the Angel of Death. If they choose no-one, nothing happens. If they choose ≥ 1 non-demon player, mark them with "countered". Later, when "countered" players are attacked by players without "countered" reminder at night, mark the victim with "attacked" and Angel of Death kills the attacker.

trouble_brute.ability: Each night, choose 2 alive (not yourself): they cannot act/wake this cycle. All effects on 1 of both (no demon, different from last cycle) are all effects of the other instead.
trouble_brute.otherNightReminder: Let the Brute choose two players (except for themself). You decide which player is unaffected and which is retargeted. The player who was made unaffected last night may not be made unaffected again. Except: the demon cannot get unaffected. Mark them with "unaffected" and "retargeted" s. Both players are similar to suspending the game, they use game actions, cannot be affected or change state/properties (even at day) & cannot wake up. The retargeted one can change (except when protected) but has no game actions either and registers covertly as dead for abilities. The retargeted player cannot die except if the unaffected player is attacked, which attacks the retargeted player.

trouble_bully.ability: Each night, ≤ 1 good player is notified, even if you are drunk/poisoned. They die if they are not publicly mad about their actual character before nominations end.
trouble_bully.otherNightReminder: After the demon killed, if a player with "bullied" reminder failed to be publicly mad about being their actual character before the nominations ended, that player dies (if the Bully is sober+healthy at the moment). Now, let the Bully choose 1 player. (If the Bully is poisoned or drunk, you may alter their choice arbitrarily.) If the bullied player is good, move the "bullied" to them and inform them about being chosen by the Bully.

trouble_clanboss.ability: Players who account for your death die tonight. You might be an Outsider. If you are, the demon learns the Outsider players.

jinxes.reason: When the Story Teller turns into the Clan Boss, executions of the Story Teller turn into executions of the nominator. The Atheist ability turns into the Heretic ability.
The Clan Boss additionally registers as Outsider to the Fang Gu.
The Clan Boss additionally registers as Outsider to the Fang Shu.

trouble_cyborg.ability: Once per cycle, whenever you publicly claim a character, it gets your (foreground) character.
trouble_cyborg.otherNightReminder: At dawn, remove the "used" reminder from the Cyborg if applicable. When the Cyborg directly/indirectly claims to be a character in the public which is different from their current 2nd ability, swap the 2nd ability with the claimed one. If swapped and the Cyborg has no "used" reminder, initialize the ability. If the swap or the invocation of the ability has produced effects on the game state, add the "used" reminder to the Cyborg. If the ability swaps during the "used" reminder, ignore the ability, also at night. The Cyborg registers as their 2nd ability else as Cyborg.

trouble_diabolo.ability: Each night, choose 2 players: they are covertly swapped as targets & (if you like) swap ability control, until dusk.
trouble_diabolo.otherNightReminder: Remove the "retarget" or "control" s. Let Diabolo choose 2 players, mark both either with "retarget" s or "control" s. (Diabolo may signal or tell you which ones.) Any player with "retarget" is swapped for the other player with "retarget" for queries & choices & effects. Players with "control" reminder additionally switch control over the character/abilities with the other player with "control" reminder (don't explicitly tell them).

trouble_equalizer.ability: Each player can nominate only once (even if they are dead).
trouble_equalizer.otherNightReminder: If a player nominates and has no "nominated" reminder, add the "nominated" to them in the Grimoire. If a player has the "nominated" reminder, they are suppressed and you have to reject the nomination.

trouble_executioner.ability: If no-one executes more than you, your team must win. You might: have 1 public Townsfolk character & be declared. You might be the demon, then 1 player dies each night.
trouble_executioner.firstNightReminder: If the Executioner should count as Demon, add the "Demon" reminder to the player in the grimoire. Initialize a counter for everybody's executing nominations. Show the Executioner their not-in-play Townsfolk ability. This ability does not interfere with bluffs of other players. Rest: See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_executioner.otherNightReminder: If someone nominated & executed players, increase their "executing nominations" count. The Executioner should register as good and as the character of their Townsfolk ability to players who receive CRISP character or alignment info (except if they generally see the actual character/alignment or you feel they should be rewarded). If the Executioner registers as Townsfolk to their own ability, they don't get Minion info. Other evils might NOT see the Executioner as minion. When the game ends – AND (optionally) if ≤ 3 players are alive – the team of the Executioner wins, if no-one nominated more executed players than the Executioner (even if the Executioner is dead).

jinxes.reason: If the Alchemist has the Executioner ability, an evil Executioner is also in play.
If the Storyteller would gain the Executioner ability, a player becomes the Executioner.
If the Executioner and Heretic/Wicked is in play, the Executioner is always declared and starts with good alignment without knowing it.
If the Executioner and Heretic/Wicked is in play, the Executioner is always declared and starts with good alignment without knowing it.
If the Ghoul is in play, no demon info shows the Executioner player. (Otherwise they could move accountability for executions onto them.)

trouble_glitcher.ability: See all first-night info, manipulate ≤ 1 & choose which is publicly declared. Each night, choose 1 player & 1 character. The player might become Imbecile or Nihilist. You might be a Demon.
trouble_glitcher.firstNightReminder: Show the Glitcher the final information of every in-play character whose player is sober+healthy. (Note, sick, unconscious or captive players don't have info.) For each character, point at the script character to show their info to the Glitcher. When done, let the Glitcher choose one of those characters and let them record a message that should be played to the affected player. Finally, let them choose the characters whose information should be made public.
trouble_glitcher.otherNightReminder: Choose 1 player & 1 character from the script (no Fabled, Loric, Traveller). If the chosen player with the chosen character would constitute a valid setup together with the other in-play characters, the player turns into an Imbecile or Nihilist with that character's ability. (E.g. you cannot add a Choirboy if a King is absent.) The chosen player turns into an imbecile if the Imbecile supports that character. Else they turn into a Nihilist. Change the character of the chosen player and move the "imbecile" or "nihilist" reminder from the previous to this player (only of both reminders is used at a time). When players become Imbecile/Nihilist they learn it. When they get rational/non-anti, they turn into their new ability's character and learn this. When the Glitcher loses their ability, remove the "imbecile" or "nihilist" reminders.

trouble_hacker.ability: Each night, you see all active jinxes & choose 1 jinx. The story teller changes the game such that this jinx toggles.
trouble_hacker.otherNightReminder: From all supported jinxes in your script, show each to the Hacker whose characters and conditions are satisfied. Now, let the Hacker choose 1 Jinx from the script. (You may note down which.) You change player properties or state in the game such that the chosen Jinx (if previously inactive) now gets active or (if previously active) gets inactive. The Alignment of characters must remain. A good character may change to a good character, an evil character may change to an evil character. Evil Minions/Demons don't turn into good. Jinxes and their text are not changed, disabled or enabled. Only the game state changes and activates/deactivates Jinxes. It may also affect other jinxes. If the Jinx cannot be (de)activated this way, the Hacker has no effect.

trouble_jailer.ability: Each night, choose 1 player (not yourself): they are captive until dusk.
trouble_jailer.otherNightReminder: Let them choose 1 player except for themself. Move the "jailed" reminder to that player. Players with "jailed" reminder may not change their player state (they cannot die) and cannot act (no waking up at all, actions at day don't work, nominations fail, they cannot vote except for Travellers).

trouble_madvirologist.ability: Each night, choose 1 alive player to get sick & register as dead until next dusk.
trouble_madvirologist.otherNightReminder: Remove any "sickened" reminder from a player at dusk. If affected player is not made sick again and lives, declare that they are not dead anymore at next dawn. Let the Mad Virologist choose 1 alive player. Add a "sickened" reminder to them and don't wake them up for their own ability until the "sickened" reminder. Als ignore their ability invokations while they are "sickened". At dawn, declare that this player is dead.

trouble_medusa.ability: Players, being mad about your evilness or this cycle's true insights on you, become "unconscious" & lose abilities from then on.
trouble_medusa.otherNightReminder: If a player has been mad about the (actual) Medusa player being evil, minion or demon: add a "incapacitated" to them. If a player shares true insights on the Medusa's properties based on any ability of this cycle, mark them with "incapacitated" if not already. Players marked "incapacitated" don't wake, can't act anymore in the game and have no abilities.

jinxes.reason: If the Storyteller would gain the Medusa ability, a player becomes the Medusa.

trouble_mephisto.ability: Once per game, choose to revive the story teller as evil, poisoned or mad. It allows them to vote.
trouble_mephisto.otherNightReminder: The Mephisto may choose to an evil, poisoned or mad story teller, but only once. Add the "evil", "mad" or "poisoned" reminder in the middle of the grimoire. Possibly also the madness condition. If "poisoned" is added, freeze the Grimoire and don't change anything until the end of the game. At dawn, declare that you revive as evil, poisoned or mad due to Mephisto.

trouble_neurohacker.ability: Each night, choose 1 to become dysinformed, then 1 to become dyseffective. Until dusk. Learn how many of both were impacted.
trouble_neurohacker.otherNightReminder: At dusk, remove any "dysinformed" and "dyseffective" reminders. Let the Neurohacker choose 1 player (including themself and dead players). Add the "dysinformed" reminder to them. Afterwards, let them choose 1 player (including the same one as before). Add the "dyseffective" reminder to them. Sleep. If you play the night ability of a player with "dysinformed" reminder and gave false info, add the "effective" reminder. If you play the night ability for a player with "dyseffective" reminder and caused false state changes, add the "effective" reminder (if not already). At dawn, wake up the Neurohacker and show them the number of players with "effective" reminder. Sleep. Remove the "effective" reminders.

trouble_panicmonger.ability: Each night, choose 1 player, then 1 good non-traveller. If the 1st executes the 2nd with ≥ 5 players alive, evil wins. All players know you are in play.
trouble_panicmonger.firstNightReminder: Declare that the Panicmonger is in play at dawn. Rest: See Other Night Reminder.
trouble_panicmonger.otherNightReminder: The Panicmonger points to a player. Add/Move the "Fury" reminder to that player. Let them point to another player who is good and not a Traveller. Add/Move the "Fear" reminder to that player. If at a day, the player with "fury" executes the player with "fear", show the Grimoire to the Panicmonger at the next night, without any Spy-/Widow-like Jinxes at play.

trouble_plague.ability: At night 3, you change to any chosen Townsfolk character. ≥ 1 Townsfolk player changes to a new Townsfolk character.
trouble_plague.otherNightReminder: At night 3, wake the Plague and let them choose any Townsfolk or Outsider character (possibly not in the script). The Plague changes to this character (but does not change alignment). Replace the Plague character in the Grimoire with a new instance of the character and flip it down to encode evil alignment (if applicable). If this happens, consider which Townsfolk players should also change (at least 1). If the plague chose a weak character, also turn the actual Townsfolk players into a weaker character. If the plague caused a significant change to the game, multiple Townsfolk may obtain strong characters (which may be duplicates).

trouble_poltergeist.ability: Each night, choose 1 different good character. While you register as it until dusk: you get its info & its actual players are Alchemist-constrained minions.
trouble_poltergeist.otherNightReminder: Let the Poltergeist choose a good character from the script. (It must be different from the last choice.) They turn into this character. Other players with this character get the "Polter" and turn them into minions with only alchemist ability. No alignment changes. Later, give info according to the Poltergeist's good character and play the Alchemist character of players with "Polter" reminder. Remove "Polter":reminders: and Alchemist-like minions, if the Poltergeist ability is removed. In this case, show players their original good character again.

trouble_president.ability: The game ends only if the majority votes to end the game. If you are deadly executed while ending the game would make you lose, evil wins.
trouble_president.otherNightReminder: The game does not end, except if someone calls for ending the game and the majority of players agree (like a call for exile). Allow any player to make a call for ending the game. Afterwards, players discuss until they signal their readiness for the ballot. The call and the ballot may happen only once per day. If most people support the call, the game ends and the winners and losers are determined per currently applicable conditions. If you are executed and die AND would lose the game during that moment (evaluating winning conditions for an imagined game end), then the evil team wins.

trouble_scaremonger.ability: Each night, you may choose 1 player (no Demon). If you do, this is declared. On the final day, the last player you chose dies, even if you died.
trouble_scaremonger.otherNightReminder: Let the Scaremonger point to a player. If it is a Demon, prompt them to choose again. Move the "Fear" next to that player. Declare that a Scaremonger chose a player at dawn. On the final dawn, if a player with "Fear" reminder lives, declare that they die and end the game.

trouble_sinisterfog.ability: Player-specific knowledge is hidden. Dead players may nominate. As many good as evil dead players may succeed in voting. Fabled don't change.
trouble_sinisterfog.otherNightReminder: When the Sinister Fog is enabled, don't declare crisp state/character/alignment changes of specific persons (story teller included). Treat dead players like alive ones but only publicly. Allow everyone to start a nomination. Don't disclose the actual vote count. You must treat votes of good deads as drugged when they exceed the number of evil deads. Deads don't use Vote Tokens. When the Sinister Fog dies, declare all publicly known state (also misregistered one when required by an ability), including specific players' public conditions/impairments and update the Townsquare.

trouble_sorcerer.ability: Each non-last night, choose 1 player OR character (not yourself) & make a game-related wish (≤ 2 predicates, no AND-like connections) about them which reverts next dusk.
trouble_sorcerer.otherNightReminder: At dusk, undo the (last) wish's non-permanent effects for the current player with "cursed" reminder. If it is not the last dusk, let the Sorcerer choose 1 player OR 1 character (but not both, no travellers and not the Sorcerer (player)). Move the "cursed" to them. The Sorcerer shows you their prepared wish (or gave it to you at the day). The wish must have ≤ 2 predicates, no AND-like connectives. Only the cursed player can be affected from the wish's effects and may only affect game state or effects that the player triggers by actions and may be conditional. It cannot directly decide about winning or losing of players. You might declare the wish towards the player publicly or privately (for balancing). Conditional effects which were declared to the player are permanent when they trigger (even if the trigger condition is gone next dusk). Write down the "‹effect›" in the Grimoire for a player who got a permanent effect. Players can only have 1 permanent effect. If they get a new one, the old one is lost. If the Sorcerer dies, remove any "cursed" s or "‹effect›" s.

trouble_spindoctor.ability: After day 1, your team members register as opposite character (not type). They know which if evil. 1 player of your team has its ability. Other players might register as its alignment.
trouble_spindoctor.otherNightReminder: At night 2, inform each of their team's members about the good (or evil) character they register as due to the Spin Doctor. Among all the Spin Doctor's team members, 1 also has the ability of the misregistered character. Mark them with "has ability". (Must be the Alchemist player with Spin Doctor ability if applicable.) Some other team members might register as the alignment of their misregistered character instead. No player misregisters as opposite alignment AND has the ability.

trouble_terminator.ability: If you nominate, execute & remove the Demon, evil wins. If you are executed deadly, 1 alive team member gets Terminator. You might register as Outsider. [≥3 evils]
trouble_terminator.firstNightReminder: Choose a not-in-play Outsider for the Terminator. Wake the Terminator to show them that they might register as that character. Add this character as reminder to the Terminator player.
trouble_terminator.otherNightReminder: If the Terminator is executed deadly, another alive player of their team gets the Terminator. If the Terminator nominates and executes, such that the Demon ability is removed (e.g. executing the Demon or turning them into a Terminator via self-execution), then the evil team wins. Usually, the Terminator should register as their Outsider: you might choose this way even at the start (preventing the Terminator from getting and being registered by minion info). The Terminator should register normally if no good abilities are in play anymore that could check the evil alignment of the Terminator. If the Terminator resurrects while another one is active, add the "self-poisoned" and treat the player as poisoned. while they have this reminder

trouble_tracker.ability: Each dawn, see all players (not yourself) whose abilities queried your registered or actual player state or properties correctly since last dawn.
trouble_tracker.otherNightReminder: Whenever the Tracker's registered or actual character, alignment or player state affected a player's ability since last dawn, add 1 "tracked" reminder to that player (if there is not already 1). At dawn, show all the players with the "tracked" reminder to the Tracker. Remove the "tracked" reminders.

trouble_voodoomaster.ability: Each night, choose 1 as puppet (not yourself), then choose 1 as projection. You cause every state change of the puppet on the projection, until dusk.
trouble_voodoomaster.otherNightReminder: At dusk, remove any "puppet" and "projection" reminder. Let the Voodoo Master choose 1 player (dead, alive or themself). Add the "puppet" reminder to them. Let them choose 1 player again (may be the same player). Add the "projection" reminder to them. Whenever the state of the player with "puppet" reminder changes, also apply the changes to the player with "projection" reminder. If you declare a state change for the Puppet, then declare it for the Projection too. Any effects that the player with "Projection" reminder receives from the player with "Puppet" reminder make the "Puppet" player accountable (even if it is the same player). Remove the "Puppet" and "Projection" reminder when the Voodoo Master loses their ability.

trouble_whisperer.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are dyseffective until dusk.
trouble_whisperer.otherNightReminder: Let them choose 1 player. Move the "whispered" reminder to that player. Players with "whispered" reminder have their final player state effects negated until next dusk (such that they differ from the unnegated state). If they chose themself, their next chosen player will have no dyseffective state until next dusk. It neither changes info they get nor any details or ability rules.

trouble_ankou.ability: On your 1st night, choose to: see minions & they you; OR kill 1 player. Each night°, choose: to (re)kill 1 player & 1 accountable alive neighbor. Learn alignment+character of who actually dies.
trouble_ankou.firstNightReminder: The Demon Info step happens before Minion Info. Show the 3 bluffs first and ask them to kill one player. If Ankou shakes the head "no", show them the Minion players. Else, if Ankou chose to kill a player, do not show the Ankou player during the Minion Info step. If any player has truely (i.e. actually) died, Ankou also learns character+alignment of this player.
trouble_ankou.otherNightReminder: Let Ankou choose 1 player to surccessively resurrect and kill. Afterwards, let them choose 1 neighbor – who registers as alive – to account for the death, not themself. The consequence of killing the death target is evaluated even if the player had been dead already. For all genuinely dead players: when they die before next dawn, inform Ankou about any new dead player's registered character+alignment.

trouble_armagon.ability: Once per game, on night ≥ 3 you can equalize evil and good alive players. Before it, evils register as good & get 1 bluff. After it, 1 evil+1 good die if no-one died at day. You are a Spy.
trouble_armagon.firstNightReminder: Give 1 not-in-play good character bluff to each Minion but no bluffs to the Armagon. Evil players register as good. At the end of the night, Armagon uses the Spy ability.
trouble_armagon.otherNightReminder: Evil players register as good during the night and day if the Armagon has no "Armageddon" reminder. If the Armagon has the "Armageddon" reminder and no-one has died last day, 1 good + 1 evil player die when the night begins. At night 3 or later, if the Armagon has no "Armageddon" reminder, wake them and allow them to choose "yes" or "no", at the beginning of the night. If they choose "yes", add the "Armageddon" to Armagon. Then you might turn alive good players into not-in-play minions and let other alive good characters die such that the number of alive good players equal the number of alive evil players. After the night, declare all players who died. At the end of the night, Armagon uses the Spy ability.

trouble_chameon.ability: Each night, you may change Minions into bluff characters OR choose 1 Townsfolk to register as minion, ELSE 1 player dies. At day, if you die, 1 alive minion gets Chameon. Alignment registers according to character.
trouble_chameon.firstNightReminder: Choose not-in-play characters as bluffs for the Chameon, 1 bluff per in-play Minion that they see in their Demon info. Add "Bluff ‹good character›" s to the Chameon player in the Grimoire. Remember: all good character players register as good, all evil character players as evil. If Chameon dies at day, another Minion-registering player becomes the Chameon.
trouble_chameon.otherNightReminder: Let the Chameon choose any pairs of a Minion character with a bluff character (see "Bluff ‹character-name›" s) but no two pairs share an equal character! If the Minion character is not in play or the bluff is already in play (from a previous transformation), the transformation fails. As alternative, the Chameon may choose 1 Townsfolk character and a Minion character. If the Townsfolk is in play and no-one registers as the chosen Minion, the Townsfolk player misregisters successfully and a "Chameon ‹minion-name›" is added to the player. If no character or registration changed, you (not Chameon) choose 1 player to die. Remember: all good character players register as good, all evil character players as evil. If Chameon dies at day, another Minion-registering player becomes the Chameon.

trouble_diabolus.ability: On your 1st night, choose which players register as evil and which as Leviathan. 1 or any more executions may happen at day, else evil wins. [Leviathan on script]
trouble_diabolus.firstNightReminder: After the demon info, let Diabolus choose any players to (mis)register as evil (even Diabolus themself). Add the "register evil" to each. Afterwards, let Diabolus choose players to misregister as Leviathan (including Diabolus themself). Add the "register Leviathan" to each. Don't let the players know. Characters that must register as specific alignment (e.g. Pandemon) won't be affected by the chosen registration. Sleep. After dawn, declare the Leviathan as you would for a Leviathan game.
trouble_diabolus.otherNightReminder: Wake Diabolus only if a Jinx needs them to choose. It only kills if a Jinx chooses so. Any player with "register evil" reminder registers as evil towards other players. Any player without "register evil" reminder registers as good towards other players. Exception: abilities like Pandemon that overwrite the registration. Any player with "register Leviathan" registers as a Demon player and Leviathan character to abilities. After dawn, declare the Leviathan as you would for a Leviathan game.

trouble_eyezero.ability: At night, any good ability info/signals are mirrored to 1 alive+evil player. Each night°, choose 1 player to die. If you die at night, another minion turns into an alive Eye Zero.
trouble_eyezero.firstNightReminder: Each night interaction of a good ability is mirrored to any (but only 1) alive+evil player immediately after the interaction. It does not reveal which player and which ability got or made the signals and doesn't distinguish Story Teller from player signals. (Like the homebrew Detective.) The mirrored playbacks should be equally distributed in number among players.
trouble_eyezero.otherNightReminder: See First Night Reminder. Let Eye Zero choose 1 player to kill. If Eye Zero is killed this night, choose an alive (otherwise dead) minion to become an alive Eye Zero (they don't kill this night). If the chosen minion was dead, they resurrect.

trouble_fangshu.ability: Each night, choose a player: they die OR the 1st chosen outsider becomes an evil Fang Shu & you die. It executes you if all goods vote only you. [+1 Outsider]
trouble_fangshu.firstNightReminder: Replace a Townsfolk with an Outsider in the setup.
trouble_fangshu.otherNightReminder: Let the Fang Shu choose 1 player. If not an outsider or if the ONCE reminder exists, add the DEAD to that player. Else, add the ONCE to the center & show the YOU ARE info token, then the Fang Shu token and a thumbs-down to the chosen. Add the DEAD to the Fang Shu. If the Fang Shu gets all remaining good votes when nominated but no other player gets good votes the same day, Fang Shu is executed (no matter the vote count).

trouble_ghoul.ability: Each night, choose 1 alive neighbour who accounts for you until dusk. Each night, choose 1 alive player (not the 2 closest good players) to kill. Choose yourself to feign death. You register like the last killed player.
trouble_ghoul.firstNightReminder: Whenever a player gets a shroud (has actually died), move the "Ghoul register" reminder to them in the Grimoire. The Ghoul registers as the character and alignment of the player with "Ghoul register" reminder. Now, let the Ghoul choose an alive neighbour and move the "Ghoul account" reminder to them in the Grimoire. The player with "Ghoul account" reminder accounts for all game actions of the Ghoul player.
trouble_ghoul.otherNightReminder: See First Night Reminder. Also: Choose 1 alive player which may not be one of the closest good players next to you. They die. If they choose themself, they are declared to have died and the Townsquare's life token is updated but they are actually still alive. If the Ghoul feigns death and only 2 players are publicly alive, the good wins if both are good. Otherwise, evil wins if the Ghoul is not executed at the same day.

trouble_gilorax.ability: Choose 1 demon character. Other Giloraxes lose theirs. 1 inactive Gilorax of Demon/Townsfolk/Outsider type (who only you & minions know) starts with impaired good character & becomes Gilorax if you are executed. [1 or 2 Giloraxes]
trouble_gilorax.firstNightReminder: Choose 1 person (player or story teller) to be the active Gilorax who gets and has only the Gilorax character token. Choose 1 player who gets the inactive Gilorax player. The inactive Gilorax player starts with a good character and has the character type of the player that they replace in the setup. (The inactive Gilorax may replace a Demon, a Townsfolk or an Outsider.) Add the Gilorax character token next to the good character token of this player. (It represents inactivity.) Now, all Gilorax players with a Demon as 2nd character lose it and die. If applicable, wake the active Gilorax player (without another character token) to let them choose an extra Demon character. Put the Gilorax token next to the new character. The Gilorax players appear in Minion Info but the inactive Gilorax player gets no Demon Info. Rest: See Other Reminder.
trouble_gilorax.otherNightReminder: At night, play the 2nd character of the Gilorax. If the Gilorax has the "inactive" reminder, the 2nd character is good which works abnormally/incorrectly. If the Gilorax was executed, remove the "inactive" of 1 other Gilorax player. If this happens while the player is still alive: wake them, show them that they are the (new) Gilorax. All other Giloraxes with a Demon as 2nd character lose it and die. Finally, let them choose 1 Demon character which replaces their old character.
trouble_gilorax.flavor:
Let me ask you an audacious question: Are you the demon?
If you ask me, well, I might be a demon… or maybe not. I might be anyone.

trouble_hydra.ability: Each night, choose 1 player to kill (not yourself). If a player deadly executes you: they get a Hydra & (if not available) a Slayer is added who turns the new Hydra evil.
trouble_hydra.otherNightReminder: At dusk, if one player deadly executed the Hydra the last day, turn them into a Hydra character with same alignment as before. Also: if there is currently no slayer who can use their ability to kill the Demon, turn the new Hydra player evil & refresh the ability of the alive slayer (telling nobody about it), if a Slayer is alive, else turn an alive good player (not the new Hydra player) into the slayer (telling only the new Slayer player about it). If no such alive good player exists to turn into a Slayer, evil wins. The Hydra + Slayer effect does not happen when the Hydra dies without execution. Now at night, wake the Hydra to choose 1 player (not themself). This player dies tonight.

trouble_kala.ability: Each night, see active Jinxes+Fabled & define new player tasks. Each night, remove, swap or add ≤1 Townsfolk or Minion + ≤1 Jinx or Fabled. Alignments are fixed. [Townsfolk + ≤ 2 Loric chosen by you;? Outsiders,? Minions, 1 Gardener]
trouble_kala.firstNightReminder: Use the Loric Gardener. While planing the game, secretly choose a player to become the Kala and who decides a list of Townsfolk that should be in play. It may only be the standard number of Townsfolk. Also allow Kala to choose at most 2 Lorics that are in play. Choose any additional outsiders and evil minions (unknown to Kala), possibly replacing some of Kala's chosen Townsfolk players. On night 1, show all active Jinxes and Fabled. If applicable, allow Kala to define any Zenomancer/Shopkeeper tasks, at most 1 task per player or character during the game. The reward may only be a 100% correct info about 1 player.
trouble_kala.otherNightReminder: Show the active Jinxes and Fabled to Kala. Kala may define new Zenomancer/Shopkeeper tasks (if applicable) but at most 1 per player or character during the game. The reward may only be 100% correct info about 1 player. Allow Kala to choose one active or inactive Fabled or Jinx that should be toggled or swapped with another Fabled or Jinx. If a Jinx changes, you change the game such that the Jinx becomes active (if it has been inactive) or inactive (if it has been active). The alignment of characters and players remains consistent. The game's change may toggle other Jinxes as well. Otherwise the Jinx toggling fails. Also let Kala choose 1 Townsfolk or Minion character and whether it should be added, removed or swapped. If the character is added, the game changes such that a player with that character lives. If the character is removed, the game changes such that a player with character dies (if it is in play). If the character is swapped, the swapped out character is removed first and (if successful) then the swapped in character is added (to the player with removed character if the swapped in character is not already in play). While Kala is alive, no player's or character's alignment may change.

trouble_ker.ability: Each night, ≥ 1 good player dies whose ability correctly interacted with you (as player) last cycle OR 1 player might die.
trouble_ker.otherNightReminder: A player detects Ker whose ability (not abnormally) interacts with or got info about specified players – the Ker player among them – or unambiguously identifies Ker. Detection is independent of noticing it. Between 1 and every detecting player die tonight (don't blow the cover early). If no-one would die you choose a dead or alive player to kill.

trouble_legionatic.ability: Each night, 1 player dies. Nominations covertly fail if only evil voted. You have +1 drunk not-in-play ability. Minions & ≥ 1 Legionatic learn the good + 1 bluff. [Most players are Legionatic,? minions]
trouble_legionatic.firstNightReminder: Devise your setup by starting with only good players and, among them, choose the standard number of good players to become a Legionatic, minus ≥ 0 players who become minions. Choose ≥ 1 Legionatic player to get Legionatic info. Add the "Legionatic" reminder to all Legionatic players. All minions also get it. For the Legionatic Info: Wake up each of them individually (e.g. clockwise). Show them all good players to be good and show them 1 unique not-in-play good character as bluff. Sleep.
trouble_legionatic.otherNightReminder: Choose a player, that player dies. At day, if a nomination gets fake – because no good players voted – treat them as normal but if it gets most of the votes, instead of moving the real "about to die" reminder to it, use the Legionatic's "About to die" reminder and remember the number of votes for both reminders. Later, declare that the player with the real "about to die" reminder is executed.

trouble_loanshark.ability: Each night, choose 1 player: alives give you 1 coin, deads 1 Vote Token. Else: they die OR (if you are minion) owe it to you. The team with most coins wins. You might be a minion. [+Shopkeeper]
trouble_loanshark.firstNightReminder: If the Loan Shark is a minion, add the "minion" reminder to the player.
trouble_loanshark.otherNightReminder: Let them choose 1 player. If alive, this player gives 1 coin to the Loan Shark. If dead, this player gives 1 vote token to the Loan Shark (which they could only use when dead, e.g. with a Mastermind). If they have no coin: the chosen player dies if the Loan Shark is a demon else (if the Loan Shark is a minion) add 1 "coin debt" or 1 "vote debt" reminder to the chosen player. A player with "coin debt" reminder who earns a coin makes the Loan Shark earn it instead and 1 reminder is removed. Analogously for the "vote debt".

trouble_neurex.ability: Each night, choose 1 player who dies next night except if they answer your optional question right. Choose 1 player to overwrite their info/signals. Minions see your bluffs & choices.
